articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System' (Digest No.48)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The author describes the INTELSAT VII satellite system design, discussing communications antennas, and the communications repeater. The spacecraft controller is considered, including attitude and orbit control, and the propulsion system and telemetry, command, and ranging are presented. Power generation, storage, and distribution are discussed and thermal control is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning aspects of the IS-VII program
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The author considers the development of the INTELSAT VII, discussing the potential deployment of satellites. Features of the IS VII, such as C-band coverage, global beam coverage, and Ku-band spot beam coverage, developed with regard to deployment, are considered. The range of INTELSAT services that will be supported by the IS-VII is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Options and alternatives on the INTELSAT VII spacecraft
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: In addition to the basic requirements for the INTELSAT VII a number of optional features and services had been identified by INTELSAT and were included in the request for proposals (RFP). These are described and include command security, spacecraft storage and retest, attitude determination and control subsystem simulator, linearisers, reduced telemetry monitoring, ion thrusters, and error corrections for inclined orbit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The communications antenna payload for INTELSAT VII comprises four antenna systems: C-band hemi/zone beam antennas, K-band spot-beam antennas, C-band spot-beam (added during contract negotiations), and C- and K-band global coverage antennas. The global coverage at both frequency bands is satisfied with the use of dual-mode Potter horns as utilised on previous INTELSAT spacecraft. The authors discuss some salient design approaches applicable to the more challenging requirements associated with C-band hemi/zone and the K-band spot-beam antennas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: Electric propulsion (EP) systems offer exhaust velocities at least an order of magnitude higher than those of chemical thrusters, so can reduce propellant masses by the same factor. For communications satellites, this benefit will be particularly valuable for north-south station-keeping (NSSK). Following an active interest in EP technology for many years, INTELSAT have assessed the possible application of ion thrusters to INTELSAT VII for NSSK, aided by proposals from the four possible prime contractors. However, these proposals were not deemed acceptable; the reasons for this are discussed, together with the characteristics of the competing EP technologies. The various factors influencing this and future decisions are considered, and INTELSAT's programme to provide the additional information needed to evaluate the application of EP to later phases is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The author gives launch vehicle requirements, and describes four proposals from Arianespace, China Great Wall Industry Corporation, General Dynamics, and Martin Marietta. Special considerations relating to the launch are given, and results of the vehicle evaluation are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The author describes the development of the INTELSAT system since 1965, discussing the first satellite, Early-Bird, and comparing it with more modern satellites such as ISVA, ISVI, and ISVII. He focuses on INTELSAT VII (ISVII), describing its features, and discusses INTELSAT's long term plans.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of the INTELSAT VII baseline spacecraft specification
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The author addresses the development of the baseline specification for the INTELSAT VII satellite and outlines the salient features of the spacecraft performance requirements. The technical requirements of the new satellite are given and the impact of these requirements is discussed. The evaluation procedure is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The INTELSAT VII attitude determination and control system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The authors discuss the control concepts of the INTELSAT VII control system, and describe the subsystem architecture. The transfer orbit mode, synchronous orbit mode, and stationkeeping mode are outlined, and inverted operation is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Filters and multiplexers for the INTELSAT VII payload
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The filtering and multiplexing requirements for this new generation of INTELSAT spacecraft have been especially demanding. Particularly for the Ku-band output multiplexer, the large number of channels to be multiplexed over the full 10.9-12.8 GHz band has meant that some challenging design problems had to be overcome before breadboard models could be successfully built and tested. The author describes C-band input multiplexers, Ku-band output multiplexers, and C-band output multiplexers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Impact of INTELSAT VII on services and Earth stations
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Intelsat VII - Another Step in the Evolution of the Global Intelsat Communications System
abstract: The author gives a review of Earth station standards and services, considering antenna size requirements. Performance objectives and performance enhancing features are discussed, and link budgets are explained.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
